Mia Chen: Heads-up — playbook automation started firing duplicate 'low-engagement' webhooks after last night's healthscore reindex. Saw ~120 duplicates in 30m.
Raj Patel: Seen it. Looks like the reindex updates health_score for accounts even without new activity, triggering the rule.
Samir Gomez: Can we add a debounce on healthscore-based triggers? e.g., require last_activity_ts within 24h OR onboarding.complete = true to avoid churn.
Mia Chen: Exactly. Also want a bounding delta: only trigger if health_score_delta >= 0.15 AND not rolled-up from batch reindex.
Julia Park: Proposed heuristic (pseudo):
```
trigger if (
  abs(new.health_score - old.health_score) >= 0.15
  AND account.last_activity_ts >= now() - 86400
  AND NOT meta.reindex_batch_id
)
```
Raj Patel: +1. Add a 15m debounce window per-account to prevent flapping when multiple updates stream in.
Samir Gomez: We should roll this as a canary: enable for 2% of accounts, monitor webhook volume and missed SLA.
Mia Chen: I'll open a small PR against cs-playbook-service with the debounce flag and canary config.
cs-ops-bot: Deploy job queued — build #5923
Julia Park: Also add a backfill script to mark recent reindex events with meta.reindex_batch_id so old entries don't retrigger.
Raj Patel: Who can own the backfill? Samir?
Samir Gomez: I can take it, aiming to run during off hours Wed night.
Mia Chen: Thanks. After canary, we'll decide if we need a longer-term rule: prefer event types (activity vs score-only) in playbook editor.
Julia Park: Noted. I'll update the runbook and add monitoring dashboard: 'cs.playbook.webhook.duplicates'.
Mia Chen: Updated tickets: CS-7890 (debounce PR), CS-7891 (backfill), CS-7892 (canary monitoring).
